title: Wassily Kandinsky: The Painter Who Heard Colours | Born 160 Years Ago Today

lines: When he heard music, he saw colours!

On this day in eighteen sixty-six,
in Moscow, Russia,
the painter Wassily Kandinsky was born.

data.name: Kandinsky

lines: He studied law and economics in Moscow,
and taught at the university.
In 1896, a university offered him a professorship.
In eighteen ninety-six, a university offered him a professorship.
But at thirty, he said no,
moved to Munich in Germany, and started over, learning to paint.
He later wrote that at a Wagner opera at the Bolshoi Theatre,
he saw all the colours in his mind.
To him, colours could sing,
and shapes had voices of their own.
That same year, Monet's painting Haystacks enchanted him too.
He told how one evening, he walked into his studio,
and saw a beautiful painting of only shapes and colours.
Up close, it was his own painting, just turned on its side!
He realized a painting didn't have to show anything at all.

In nineteen eleven, he wrote a book, Concerning the Spiritual in Art:
art must express the inner life.
He also formed The Blue Rider with friends,
and began painting only lines, circles and patches of colour,
becoming one of the first abstract painters.
Later, he taught at the Bauhaus school,
using circles, triangles and squares.
In 1933, the Nazis shut the Bauhaus, and he moved to France.
In nineteen thirty-three, the Nazis shut the Bauhaus, and he moved to France.
In 1937, they branded his art degenerate.
In nineteen thirty-seven, they called his art degenerate, and pulled it from German museums.
He died near Paris in 1944, at seventy-seven.
He died near Paris in nineteen forty-four, at the age of seventy-seven.
Today, his paintings hang in museums all over the world,
and shape posters, design and countless artists.
His question for you:
When you listen to music, what colours do you see?
